issues.display_title: Issue #4143: Show All / Hide All Button
issues.main_description_html:
Context

One button only — whichever action makes sense right now. Both act on every tour in the account.

Situation (account-wide) Button reads
Some hidden, or all hidden Show All
Every tour visible Hide All

The state is decided by the account-wide counts, not by what's on screen. With a search active the customer may see three tours and a button that affects four hundred — the wording has to make the scope unmistakable.

Both actions ask for confirmation first. Keep the modal plain — a short line saying what is about to happen, cancel and confirm. Nothing else.

Design

Wording and layout are not specified here — use the ui-ux-pro-max plugin. The result goes to UI or Product for review before merge.

Acceptance criteria

  • Only one button is ever shown, with the correct label for the account-wide state
  • The label does not change when the customer searches or changes page
  • The wording makes clear the action covers every tour, not just what's visible
  • Both Show All and Hide All ask for confirmation before anything changes
  • Cancelling changes nothing
  • Unavailable while the list is loading or a change is saving
  • After the action, every card on screen and the count reflect the new state
  • Reviewed and approved by UI or Product
  • All new wording goes through the translation layer, English first

Depends on

  • GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1704

issues.display_title: Issue #4144: Turn the Portfolio Settings Sidebar Into a Wizard
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Four screens currently sit in a flat list in an order nobody would use — Template first (src/components/organism/SideMenu/PortfolioMenu.jsx). New order:

Step 1         Step 2             Step 3               Step 4
About     →    Center Location →  Featured Business →  Template
(required)     (required)         (optional)           (required)

The Photographer Directory signup already uses the same model (PhotographerNoviceMenu.jsx) — follow its look so the two feel like one product. That menu itself is not touched.

The sidebar is what enforces the order. Gating exists to guide people through setup the first time; it must never become a permanent obstacle.

Which steps are complete comes from the API as setup_steps — a flag per step. This issue reads those flags and decides what is open; it does not work completion out for itself.

Step Available when
About always
Center Location About done
Featured Business About and Center Location done
Template About and Center Location done

The flags come from GET /portfolios/setup-steps, added by GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1709. This issue is blocked until that endpoint exists.

On arrival, land the customer on their first unfinished step. Once, when Portfolio Settings opens — after that, never interfere with where they navigate.

Design

The look of each step state is not specified here — use the ui-ux-pro-max plugin. The result goes to UI or Product for review before merge.

Acceptance criteria

  • Sidebar shows four steps in the new order
  • Each step shows as done / available / locked
  • Later steps are locked until About and Center Location are complete
  • Clicking a locked step does nothing at all — no navigation, no error
  • A customer who has finished setup can move between all four steps freely
  • Still works in the slide-out menu on small screens
  • Works in dark mode
  • Opening Portfolio Settings lands the customer on their first unfinished step
  • A brand-new account lands on About, a fully configured one lands on Template
  • The redirect runs once per visit and never interrupts deliberate navigation
  • Checked against a real existing account with partially filled About details
  • Reviewed and approved by UI or Product
  • All new wording goes through the translation layer, English first

Depends on

  • GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1709

issues.display_title: Issue #4145: About Step — Focus the First Empty Required Field
issues.main_description_html:
Context

src/pages/Portfolio/Settings/About.jsx. The five-field validation already exists (:60-70) and refs are already attached to every input (DetailInfo.jsx:88-235) — but nothing ever focuses them, so the customer has to hunt for what's missing.

The save button on this step becomes Next — it saves, then moves forward. The button is never greyed out: a greyed-out button tells a customer they can't proceed but not why. Let the message name what's missing instead.

Blocked message: "Fill in company name, email, phone, background colour, and page title to continue." — name only the fields actually missing.

Acceptance criteria

  • The button reads Next and is never disabled
  • Pressing Next scrolls to and focuses the first empty required field
  • The message names only the fields actually missing
  • With everything filled, Next saves and moves to Center Location

issues.display_title: Issue #4147: Featured Business Step — Explanation Panel and Skip
issues.main_description_html:
Context

src/pages/Portfolio/Settings/Business.jsx. The maximum of three and the duplicate rejection already work — but the screen has never explained them, so the rules only surface as a button that mysteriously stops working.

Two things to build here: the explanation panel, and skipping the step.

A third one is small — the add-featured modal (Components/CreateFeaturedBusiness.jsx) has to ask the API to leave out businesses that are already featured, so they never reach the dropdown in the first place. The backend issue supplies the flag.

What the panel has to get across

Straight from PRD 6.6:

  • What a featured business is — a business highlighted prominently at the top of the public portfolio page
  • A maximum of three can be featured
  • The same business can't be added twice

Design

Exact wording and layout are not specified here — use the ui-ux-pro-max plugin. Final copy is still open per PRD 11, so placeholders are fine during build. The result goes to UI or Product for review before merge.

Acceptance criteria

  • Explanation panel covers all three points above
  • The add-featured search asks the API to exclude already-featured businesses
  • An already-featured business never appears in the dropdown, even searched by exact name
  • The button reads Next and is never disabled
  • Next moves to Template with zero featured businesses added
  • Reviewed and approved by UI or Product
  • All new wording goes through the translation layer, English first

  • GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1710

issues.display_title: Issue #4148: Template Step — Save, View Button, and No Dead Buttons
issues.main_description_html:
Context

This is the last step, so the button stays Save rather than Next — there is nowhere further to go.

The button is never greyed out. Today Apply goes dead when a non-Pro customer selects a premium template (Template.jsx:64) — that comes off and a message takes its place, so the customer learns why they can't proceed instead of finding a button that does nothing.

Once a template is saved, a View button appears next to Save and opens the public portfolio in a new tab. The same button already exists on the portfolio list header (Portfolio.jsx:298-311) — reuse the URL it builds. It must also show for customers who saved a template previously, not only in the moment right after saving.

Acceptance criteria

  • The button reads Save and is never disabled
  • A non-Pro customer selecting a premium template gets a message, not a dead button
  • The View button appears on load for anyone with a saved template
  • View opens the correct portfolio address in a new tab
  • All new wording goes through the translation layer, English first

issues.display_title: Issue #4179: fix(payment): send period when creating a PayPal overlay order
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

PaypalMethod builds the create-order payload in src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaypalMethod.jsx:103-113:

data: {
  product_name: productName,
  first_name: billingInfo.first_name,
  last_name: billingInfo.last_name,
  email: billingInfo.billing_email,
  country: billingInfo.country,
  moderation_id: mid || undefined,
  state: billingInfo.state || undefined,
  tour_key: tourKey || undefined,
}

period is missing, and it determines the price. The overlay unlock costs cost * period; the API defaults it to 1 when absent, so PayPal only holds one year. PaymentV2.jsx:500 then sends period: billingInfo?.period at capture and the user is granted that many years.

PaymentRightSection.jsx:81 already shows the period selector for unlock_gothru_overlay and unlock_google_overlay, and OrderDetails.jsx:480 already multiplies the displayed price by it. So the customer sees the multi-year total in the order summary and is charged for one year.

Change

  • Pass period into PaypalMethod and include it in the create-order payload for the overlay products, matching what PaymentV2 already sends at capture.
  • Keep the create and capture payloads in sync — a field that moves the price has to be present in both, with the same value.
  • Surface the new rejection from the API. Today onError shows a generic purchase failure; a price mismatch should tell the user to reload rather than retry the same order.

Acceptance

  • The create-order request for fov / gov carries the same period the capture request will send.
  • Buying a multi-year overlay charges the multi-year total shown in the order summary.
  • No new client-supplied pricing input is introduced.

Deploy order

This has to ship before or together with the API-side amount check (GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1728). If the API guard lands first, the dashboard is still sending period only at capture, the two amounts disagree, and every multi-year overlay purchase is rejected.

Files

  • src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaypalMethod.jsx
  • src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaymentRightSection.jsx
  • src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaymentV2.jsx

issues.display_title: Issue #4185: Add Countly analytics to the dashboard
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Add Countly analytics to the dashboard so we can see how people actually use it — which pages they visit, how long they stay, and where they run into errors. Today we have no usage data at all, so product decisions are guesswork.

Requirements

  • Track visits and sessions automatically once a user opens the dashboard.
  • Track every page the user moves to, including navigation inside the app that does not reload the browser.
  • Track clicks, scrolling, outbound links, and JavaScript errors automatically.
  • Attach the logged-in user to their activity (name, email, language, account type, subscription) so reports can be broken down per user and per plan.
  • Provide a simple way for developers to record extra events later (for example: tour published, subscription purchased) without reworking the setup.
  • The analytics server address and app key are configuration, not hardcoded values, so staging and production can point to different Countly apps.
  • If the configuration is missing or empty, the dashboard runs exactly as before and sends nothing. No errors, no blocked builds.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Opening the dashboard starts a session in Countly.
  • Moving between pages shows up as separate page views.
  • Logging in links the activity to that user's profile in Countly.
  • Errors that happen in the dashboard appear in Countly.
  • With the configuration removed, the dashboard behaves normally and no data is sent.
  • The server address works whether or not it is written with a trailing slash.
  • No visible change to the interface and no change to existing features.

Out of scope

  • Consent / GDPR opt-in screen.
  • Custom event tracking for specific features (to be added per feature as needed).
  • Remote config and performance monitoring (APM).

issues.display_title: Issue #4209: [Countly P0] Harden privacy-safe foundation, identity, and page views
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Harden the existing Countly foundation so all product analytics pass through one privacy-safe boundary and remain reliable across authentication and SPA navigation.

Scope

  • Centralize policy in src/utils/countly.js.
  • Keep Countly configuration environment-driven and no-op safely when configuration is absent.
  • Use a pseudonymous identity; never send email, name, raw user ID, or other PII as event segmentation.
  • Tag activity with normalized actor_type so support activity can be separated from customer funnels.
  • Reset/rotate Countly identity on every logout and session-clearing path without merging the old identity.
  • Normalize dynamic SPA paths for both application page views and the Countly SDK view.
  • Allow only stable, low-cardinality properties and sanitized reason codes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Identity behavior is covered for login, logout, and forced session clearing.
  • Dynamic route identifiers are absent from recorded page paths.
  • Support and customer activity are filterable by actor_type.
  • Missing Countly configuration does not break the dashboard.
  • Privacy-focused tests prove that disallowed values are dropped.

References

  • Related implementation: #4208
  • Existing base integration: #4185
  • PM-approved catalog: docs/product/countly-feature-tracking-review.md
  • Shipped inventory: docs/product/countly-p0-event-inventory.md

This issue is intentionally linked without an auto-close keyword.

issues.display_title: Issue #4227: Implement Tour List Sorting State and API Query Bindings
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Add sorting to the "My Tours" list and bind the selected option to the page URL and tour-list API request.

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. Show a Sort control beside Filter with these values: size, date_created, date_modified, and alphabetically.
  2. Keep the active sort in page state and the sort_by URL query parameter. No sort is selected by default, selecting the active option again clears it, and empty or unsupported values are removed from the URL.
  3. Send sort_by only when active in GET /v1/tours/list. Do not send a sort_order parameter.
  4. Reset pagination to page 1 when sort changes while preserving active search, tour type, and hashtag filters.
  5. Preserve the active sort across pagination, page-size changes, reloads, and action-triggered refetches. Keep bulk-action filter parameters unchanged.
  6. On mobile, render Search on a full row with Filter and Sort side-by-side below it. At md and larger, render Search, Filter, and Sort on one row.
  7. Add Sort labels and option translations to all supported locales.
